scope: Corollary 3.37 (Uniform crepancy parameter; no termination assertion) of the manuscript “Log abundance for compact Kähler spaces under logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity” (preprints/Log-abundance-for-compact-Kahler-spaces-under-logarithmic-Iitaka-subadditivity-October-6-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 034 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 46adc5be1070213b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 57. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose additionally that the working spaces are d-dimensional klt spaces, that αi are nef, and that the ordinary canonical negative-ray length bound 0 < −KXi · C ≤ 2d is available. For a fixed real number t > 2d/δ, every negative extremal ray chosen in an existing (KXi + tαi)-program is αi-trivial. If the steps are projective ordinary canonical steps, Lemma 3.36 therefore applies inductively with this same value of t. If α0 is not big and α0 − c1(KX0 ) is big, then KXi + tαi remains non-pseudo-effective along these crepant steps. Consequently a terminating such program ends with a Mori fibre contraction. This corollary does not assert that the requisite contractions exist or that the program terminates.
